stories.title: Senior Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
stories.summary: Hamas said a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli airstrike, with the Israeli military confirming his death. Samir Abu Younis, 53, the commander of the Rafah brigade, was killed yesterday, the Palestinian militant group's armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades, has said. The Israeli military said it had killed Mr Abu Younis in a strike in southern Gaza overnight, adding that he had led the Rafah brigade since his predecessor, Nael Abu Obeid, was killed on 15 September. Medics said Mr Abu Younis was killed and others were wounded in an airstrike that targeted him in a street in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis in southern Gaza. Hamas said Mr Abu Younis joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and had held several senior operational roles in Rafah before becoming commander of the brigade. His funeral will be held this afternoon in Khan Younis, Hamas said.

stories.title: Refereeing calls a source of irritation after Linz loss
stories.summary: Heimir Hallgrimsson admitted that a litany of refereeing decisions left him "unhappy" in the wake of his Republic of Ireland side's UEFA Nations League defeat in Austria on Saturday night. The Boys in Green succumbed to a second-half winner from substitute Sasa Kalajdzic as they suffered a 1-0 defeat in Linz. But one particular flashpoint involving Kalajdzic exemplified Hallgrimsson's misgivings with some of the decisions made by the officiating team. In the 69th minute, the six-foot-seven striker's elbow appeared to connect with the top of Dara O'Shea's forehead whilst the two were contesting an aerial ball. While the Bosnian referee Irfan Peljto awarded Ireland a free kick, no card was issued. "(O'Shea) said (to the referee) that I elbowed him but I said he pulled me back so that's why I came in this weird position and also I'm a little taller than him so my arm is automatically in a different position and awkward position for him but it wasn't a bad intention and not on purpose. I told him that," said the LASK Linz target man.

stories.title: Fielding says he has had no contact with Brand in years
stories.summary: The Great British Bake Off presenter Noel Fielding said he has had "no contact" with Russell Brand "for many years". It comes after Brand was jailed for 10 and a half years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others and has been accused of abusing his celebrity status to prey on women. In a statement issued to The Sun, Fielding said: "I was horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand's crimes, which I was completely unaware of until they became public knowledge. My thoughts are with the women whose courage brought him to justice. "I appeared on TV, radio and live charity shows with him, and whilst we played it up for the cameras and in the media, I considered it a professional relationship, rather than a personal one. I have had no contact with him for many years. "Looking back at some of the jokes I made alongside him I was appalled. They were horrible and inappropriate, and I very much regret them." Brand and Fielding appeared together on Channel 4’s Big Fat Quiz Of The Year and performed charity gigs together as The Goth Detectives.

stories.title: Flight chaos in US continues after nationwide shutdown
stories.summary: US air travel is not expected to return to normal schedules until later today, the head of the FAA said, as the aviation system gradually recovers from a nationwide flight shutdown that officials blamed on routine maintenance gone awry. As of 9:35pm ET (2.35am Irish time), airlines had cancelled more than 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000, according to FlightAware, an aviation website. That followed about 9,200 flights cancelled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications. FlightAware said 875 flights scheduled for today were already cancelled. Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford said that he expected airline operations to largely return to normal later. He also apologised for the disruption, adding that the system remains stable.

stories.title: Irish scrum improving but the true test awaits v the Boks
stories.summary: While Ireland's scrum has been dominant in the first two games of this Nations Championship window, the true test of Ireland's setpiece is in store next week. The setpiece was the only consistent element of last night's 43-15 win against Fiji at Aviva Stadium, as their lineout and scrum served up a 100% return, with the scrum in particular leading to four penalties, a platform from which Andy Farrell's side could grind their way to an otherwise unconvincing win. With the world champion Springboks coming to Dublin next Saturday evening, we will see just how real those improvements have been. Twelve months ago, Rassie Erasmus's side humiliated Ireland's scrum in their 24-13 win at the Aviva. The Boks drew six scrum penalties and four additional penalty advantages from that avenue alone last year, while Andrew Porter and Paddy McCarthy were both sent to the sin-bin, as Ireland were on the receiving end of a pummelling up front. While the Springboks come to Dublin this week off the back of a dramatic 21-19 defeat to France, the way they ripped open the French scrum in Paris sent an ominous message to Ireland, and the rest of the world.

stories.title: Papa Roach raise over €5,000 for Pieta suicide prevention
stories.summary: US rock band Papa Roach raised over €5,000 for Pieta, the Irish organisation dedicated to suicide prevention, on their recent trip to Dublin as part of the band's on-going campaign. The band, whose hits include Last Resort and Forever, played the 3Arena on the 3rd of November and presented a cheque for the funds raised to backstage at the gig. They have donated over $750,000 since 2023 in their commitment to suicide prevention and self-harm support. "This return to Dublin was long overdue, and the fans showed us why," said front man Jacoby Shaddix. "We can’t thank them enough for helping us give back the energy at the live show and give back to support an important cause." stories.title: Farrell admits scoreline 'flattered' Ireland in Fiji win
stories.summary: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell admits his side were flattered by their 28-point winning margin against Fiji, but insists their 43-15 win was good preparation for what's to come with the physicality of South Africa next week. A 26-0 second half saw Ireland pull away from Jake White's side after an error-strewn opening 40, where Ireland were 17-15 in front and left multiple tries behind them. And while the head coach acknowledged those errors, he was pleased with how his side put the game to bed. "I'm pleased to get the win, especially the scoreline," Farrell said. "I thought it flattered us a little bit, but having said that, you've got to work for those points and find a way, especially when after 25 minutes you're down by five points against a side that's playing pretty well as far as the physical nature of the game." Fiji, now under the coaching of former World Cup winning Springbok boss Jake White, were well in the game for the first 55 minutes before Andrew Porter grabbed Ireland's fifth try from which they never looked back.

stories.title: BBC removes Room On The Broom film featuring Walliams
stories.summary: The BBC has removed the 2012 film adaptation of Julia Donaldson's children’s book Room On The Broom featuring David Walliams. Walliams, a best-selling author and former Britain’s Got Talent judge, 55, was named as part of an alleged sexual misconduct investigation by The Guardian and ITV News on Tuesday. One woman described her alleged encounter with Walliams when she was 15 as "sexual assault", while multiple women accused him of "grooming" them when they were teenagers. Walliams denies any wrongdoing. On Friday, the Metropolitan Police said it had received a number of non-recent "serious" sex offence allegations against him "in recent days". Earlier in the week, the BBC said it was carrying out a review of "all material" featuring and written by Walliams on its platforms and was in the process of "removing" some. One such show to be removed is the animated adaptation of Room On The Broom, in which Walliams voices a frog alongside Gillian Anderson as the witch and Simon Pegg as the narrator.

stories.title: Determined Pope travels to Latin America after surgery
stories.summary: At the end of the October, the Vatican confirmed that Pope Leo XIV's apostolic trip to Latin America would proceed on 6 November, according to a previously published programme. The confirmation came just 13 days after the pope underwent surgery at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital to remove a malignant tumour from his right lung. There were concerns about possible health challenges resulting from changing altitudes in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, but doctors gave him the green light to travel. Rather than postponing the trip, the Pope was reportedly determined to keep his commitment and return to the continent where he spent two decades as a missionary priest and a bishop. Robert Prevost first went to Peru as an Augustinian missionary in 1985 where he spent almost half of his priestly life before Pope Francis called him to Rome in 2023 to head the Vatican’s Dicastery for Bishops. Latin America is home to around 40% of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics, but the Catholic proportion of the region's population has shrunk in recent years.

stories.title: Parrott: Ireland's promotion hopes still in our hands
stories.summary: Troy Parrott says Ireland can still achieve what they want to with a victory against Kosovo on Tuesday following last night's defeat to Austria. Sasa Kalajdzic got the only goal in Linz to secure automatic promotion for the Austrians, and leave the Boys in Green needing a win at Aviva Stadium to keep their promotion hopes alive. That can only come via a play-off, with the added carrot of second place securing a higher seeding for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw. Troy Parrott worked hard but, on a frustrating night, he couldn't find the back of the net as Ireland fell to their second defeat of the Nations League campaign. "We fell short today, but we still have a big chance on Tuesday to do what we want to do. "Me, Jack (Moylan) and Adam (Idah) have been doing well together in the last couple of games, so it was expected from us that we were going to play together again."

Jones was partnered with Aljaz Skorjanec, West with Alexis Warr, Giedroyc with Neil Jones, Clark with Amy Dowden, and Cox with Julian Callion. Giedroyc was left out of breath as she and Jones performed a humorous routine to The Floral Dance by Terry Wogan, in tribute to the show’s late presenter. The dancers were then all awarded a 10 by a panel of child judges and Pudsey Bear.

stories.title: New measures set to target money laundering
stories.summary: The Tánaiste Simon Harris has announced new measures to improve transparency around beneficial ownership and to strengthen the anti-money laundering regime in Ireland. A beneficial owner is the real person or people who own or control a company or legal entity, even if it's registered under another name, broker or company structure. The measures are aimed at helping people with a legitimate interest, including journalists and civil society academics, to find out who is behind companies, trusts and certain financial vehicles. Under the new criteria those who can demonstrate an eligible interest may apply for access to specified information held on Ireland's beneficial ownership register. The new legitimate-interest arrangements implement relevant provisions of the EU’s Sixth Anti-Money Laundering Directive. The government said the arrangements are part of a wider drive to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing, as well as protecting the integrity of the country's financial system.

stories.title: Hallgrimsson stresses small details after 'painful' loss
stories.summary: Heimir Hallgrimsson said it was "painful" to take nothing from the game after Ireland's 1-0 defeat in Linz, the manager stressing that the team want to "stop building and start winning". After an adventurous display in an open game, with Ireland dominating in terms of possession and chances for large swathes of the first half, the visitors were undone by a scrappy late goal from a corner. Substitute Sasa Kalajdzic, who caught Dara O'Shea with an elbow to the face shortly after coming on, poked the ball from a yard out after Michael Gregoritsch headed the ball across goal from the back post. The corner had been needlessly conceded when Nathan Collins, otherwise impressive in defence, turned into trouble when in possession, losing the ball in a dangerous area, with the resulting effort yielding the fateful corner. Ireland piled on the pressure in search of an equaliser. They could easily have scored a few times in either half, with the excellent Troy Parrott forcing a couple of saves from Alexander Schlager, while numerous dangerous crosses throughout the game went unmet by Irish attackers. The Ireland manager acknowleged it was annoying that they didn't find a deserved late equaliser but he noted that whether they drew or lost, it didn't change the equation much in terms of the group.

stories.summary: Rapper Strange Boy and T.A. Narrative are among the acts who will play an all-Limerick Sessions for Oblivion show later this Month with further gigs in Belfast and Dublin to follow. The free show at Dolan's in Limerick on the 26th of November will also feature post-hardcore/shoegaze/grunge band Mother of Pearl and alt-rock/metal crossover act Layen. Sessions From Oblivion will also host new shows in Dublin and Belfast in what will be their first ever all 32-county event. As always with SFO live shows, the order of acts playing is picked out of a hat on the day and not announced so gig goers are encouraged to show up at the start or they will miss the act they really want to see.

stories.title: Ireland face must-win game after narrow loss in Austria
stories.summary: The Republic of Ireland are facing into a must-win clash against Kosovo as their UEFA Nations League promotion hopes took a hit despite a gutsy display against Austria in Linz. Heimir Hallgrimsson's side impressed at times, especially in a first half in which they warmed to their task and took the game to their hosts at times. However, it was substitute Sasa Kalajdzic who pounced with 11 minutes of normal time to go to ultimately settle the contest at the Raiffeisen Arena. The Boys in Green will return to action in three days' time at Aviva Stadium needing to beat Kosovo in order to leapfrog the Balkan nation into second and thereby claim a promotion play-off spot and boost their seedings for the next European Championship qualifiers. A draw will consign Ireland to another campaign in League B, whilst a defeat could open the door for bottom side Israel should they beat the promoted Austrians on Tuesday. That stance was reflected in a starting XI that saw the attack-minded Finn Azaz deployed in a deeper role, just as he had in the 2-2 draw against the same opponents at Aviva Stadium on 1 October.

stories.title: Beirne admits Ireland need to improve on 'clunky' display
stories.summary: Ireland captain Tadhg Beirne said the team have plenty to improve upon after a "clunky" display against Fiji, with world champions South Africa arriving in Dublin next weekend. Leading by just two points at half-time, Ireland ran in four tries in the second half and kept the Fijians scoreless to win on a comfortable 43-15 scoreline in the finish. Robert Balacoune and Tommy O'Brien both scored two tries apiece, with Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and Nick Timoney getting over for the others as Ireland made it four wins from five in the competition. Nonetheless, Beirne feels they struggled for momentum at times, though he credits much of that to the Fijians. "We didn't get the momentum we wanted to. That's a credit to Fiji in that they got on top of us at times and then we got a little bit desperate and gave away a good few penalties. "That's something we're going to have to look at because we're playing a very good side next week.

stories.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship 'catch'
stories.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX pulled off the first-ever "catch" of a spaceship, a technical feat that shows the feasibility of fully reusable rockets and brings affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality. The Starship emerged from a cloudy sky after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth's atmosphere, then descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical "chopstick arms" above Launch Pad 2. The success marked a milestone in the space industry's decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems - a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. "That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes," SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with 1977 soft rock hit "Baby Come Back" serving as the soundtrack of the nerve-wracking final descent on SpaceX's official livestream. It was the 15th test flight of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket system.

stories.title: Top Tip: How fast fashion revitalised dumpster diving
stories.summary: For all its ills, social media has at least played a positive role in the revival of some out-of-favour practices and past-times; from niche crafts to long-neglected recipes. But it's also helping to rehabilitate certain activities – including some that would previously have been seen as the preserve of the most desperate. Dumpster diving certainly fits that bill. While the practice of rooting through bins and skips would long have been - fairly or unfairly - with poverty, today it is experiencing something of a boom in popularity. That is in part due to the cost-of-living crisis, which has made many people take significant steps to reduce their expenses. But that same pressure has also seen people search for ways to earn more money, and many have stumbled upon a community of dumpster diving influencers, who post regularly about their hauls and brag openly about their earnings. One such influencer - 31-year-old Carter Stevens – claims to be making somewhere in the region of $140,000 a year from dumpster diving. Others talk about slightly more modest – but nonetheless impressive – earnings in the tens of thousands. Of course this is social media we’re talking about – so followers might not quite be getting the most accurate impression of what’s involved.

stories.title: Philippines win inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia
stories.summary: A Filipino teenager has won the first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia with a song backing women's empowerment. Carmelle Collado, 19, took the title in Bangkok in a smaller version of the famous European extravaganza - which featured 11 acts. Eurovision bosses launched the competition earlier this year aiming to "evolve Eurovision together with Asia". Eurovision previously tried to expand internationally with the American Song Contest, however, it only lasted one year amid poor viewing figures. Collado’s song Sobra-Sobra, which mixes English and Tagalog, secured the most points from the public vote and jury of peers. It has been described as a tribute to Filipino women and includes lyrics such as "When I show my strength too bad you can’t stop me" and "I won’t put myself down".

stories.title: Dublin businesses seek compensation after summit impact
stories.summary: The sun was bouncing off the Liffey as smiling world leaders arrived at Dublin's Convention Centre for this week's EU Summit. Warnings about heightened security and road closures were well signposted. There were some protests but little to no violence, and the Government and organisers will likely be very happy about how the week panned out. But not everyone is smiling. City centre business owners have taken a financial hit, as many Dubliners heeded the warnings and stayed at home to avoid the disruption. It was particularly difficult for businesses located inside the Garda security cordon around the convention centre, like the Grafton Barber shop in the IFSC. "We had three days where customers didn't have access to the shop," said the IFSC franchise owner Fabian Pollard. "We had to go out and bring the customers from the barrier into the shop and business was probably down about 50%," he added. Staff in the shop were also impacted by getting less hours because of the reduced business, but Mr Pollard said they were quite accepting. "They understood, but they all have their own lives and they have their financial commitments, so it's still a hit for them", he said.

stories.title: Post-mortem completed on man's body found in Phoenix Park
stories.summary: Gardaí investigating the discovery of a man's body in Dublin's Phoenix Park say a post-mortem examination has been completed. They say a formal murder investigation has not begun at this time. Gardaí say they are continuing to investigate all the circumstances surrounding the discovery of the man's body in the vicinity of the Wellington Monument in Phoenix Park yesterday morning. He has been identified as a man in his 40s who was originally from Eastern Europe but had been living in Ireland for several years. A post-mortem examination was completed at Dublin City Mortuary in Whitehall today. Gardaí say the results are not being released for operational reasons. An incident room has been established at Finglas Garda Station under the direction of a Senior Investigating Officer.

stories.title: Second half flurry gives Ireland unconvincing win v Fiji
stories.summary: Ireland warmed up for next week's visit of South Africa with a 43-15 bonus-point win against Fiji, but Andy Farrell's side will need a significant improvement when the world champions come to town next week. If last week's performance against Argentina set the 'new standards' for this Ireland team, Andy Farrell's side fell well short of that mark, and while they outscored the Fijians 26-0 in the second half, it was far from a vintage display. The sloppiness of their summer in Australia and New Zealand returned tonight, seeing three potential first-half tries chalked off, which allowed Fiji stay in the game for the first hour. Also concerning was their discipline, which consistently struggled as soon as they were pinned into their own 22 with Fiji taking advantage in the opening half to score a pair of tries from Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato, before Ben Volavola added a penalty on 40 minutes following Tadhg Beirne's yellow card. A Tommy O'Brien try and two from the excellent Rob Baloucoune had Ireland 17-15 in front after the break, and they looked a far better side after it, with Rónan Kelleher, Andrew Porter, O'Brien and Nick Timoney all crossing to score, while keeping their opponents scoreless. If there was a big positive for Farrell it will have been the Irish scrum, which dominated throughout, and while the Springboks will present a far greater setpiece challenge, it's a timely confidence boost for John Fogarty's scrummaging unit.

stories.summary: People in Derry have attended an anti-racism rally in the city following violent attacks on three members of the Nigerian community. One of the victims was left with a broken leg after he was beaten with an iron bar. A woman had her car windscreen smashed and a man was assaulted in a pub. The attacks all happened in the Bond Street area of the city within a short time of one another last Sunday. Police have said they believe they may be linked and were racially motivated. Derry Trades Council organised the rally at Ebrington Square in the city at lunchtime today and heard from the man whose leg was broken - a healthcare worker.

stories.title: Record homeless level revealed as EU red carpet rolled up
stories.summary: When the big guns are in town, the last thing a government wants to point to is the stain on its copybook. This week, the distraction of events at the Convention Centre enabled it to quietly publish an action plan on child and family homelessness as well as the latest homeless figures. Nothing to see here EU friends, just over 18,000 in emergency accommodation and an action plan to tackle the record number of homeless children and families. In the last 12 years, homeless figures have grown from almost 4,000 to over 18,000. When the Department of Housing began publishing its monthly homeless figures in 2014, there were 749 homeless children. Today, almost 6,000 children live in emergency accommodation - the impact on their growth and development, exhaustively documented. An action plan to tackle the issue was proposed last year when the Government delivered a housing plan up to 2030.

stories.title: Bishop supports call for talks on declining birth rate
stories.summary: The Bishop of Achonry and Elphin has supported the call for a national discussion on declining birth rate, abortion figures and the long-term implications for families, healthcare services and the sustainability of the welfare state by the group Healthcare Professionals for Life. Bishop Kevin Doran, who is chairman of the Catholic Bishops' Council for Life, challenged what he described as attempts to "do away" with the three-day waiting period for women seeking abortions in Ireland. stories.title: Wales end 73-year wait with epic victory over All Blacks
stories.summary: Wales ended 73 years of hurt against New Zealand and shredded world rugby's form book by winning an epic Nations Championship encounter 35-28 at the Principality Stadium. The All Blacks had reeled off 34 successive victories at Wales’ expense since being beaten by them in 1953, but Steve Tandy’s team gloriously achieved mission improbable after a Cardiff classic. Three times Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time in history they scored five tries against New Zealand, but ultimately it was heroic defensive work that denied the visitors. First-half tries from Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake and Archie Griffin – all converted by Sam Costelow – put Wales in charge, although New Zealand clawed it back to 21-21 as Cortez Ratima, Wallace Sititi and Fehi Fineanganofo all touched down, with Richie Mo’unga booting three conversions. All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie made eight changes from the side that swept past Scotland in their previous Nations Championship game, and such an approach ultimately backfired spectacularly, with Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit adding further Wales scores that Costelow converted. A crowd of 55,152 could scarcely believe what had unfolded, and there were incredible scenes of wild celebration with players in tears as Wales began taking in arguably the most famous win of their 145-year Test match history.

stories.title: Microsoft services fully restored after global outage
stories.summary: Microsoft has said that services have fully recovered across Teams, Outlook ⁠and its other products, ending a global outage that crippled online communications for businesses and governments for over 24 hours. "We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions," the company posted on X. Microsoft had said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant, and that it was not aware of any malicious activity, ruling out AI as the cause. Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings. Disruption was seen in Ireland and the UK from around 6pm on Thursday evening.

stories.title: Netanyahu renews call for unity government with opponent
stories.summary: Israel's caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reiterated his call for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse. The latest exchange comes as Mr Eisenkot is negotiating to form a government after being tasked with becoming prime minister. A meeting with Mr Eisenkot "only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government" to guarantee Israel's security, Mr Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could "eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all". He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel "as a state for the Jewish people". It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would "not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us". The outgoing prime minister warned against Mr Eisenkot's plan to form a minority government, presented as a "national emergency government".
